concepts.title: Cell Theory and an Overview of the Cell
concepts.section: 8.1 A Cell is defined as, 8.2 Cell Theory
concepts.definition: The cell is the fundamental structural and functional unit of all living organisms; Schleiden and Schwann proposed the cell theory and Virchow added that cells arise from pre-existing cells through cell division omnis cellula e cellula.
concepts.key_idea: Cell biology developed with the microscope: from Robert Hooke's cork observation to the unified cell theory that all living beings are made of cells.
question_patterns: state the cell theory and who proposed it
what did virchow add to the cell theory
why is the cell called the structural and functional unit of life
describe robert hooke's observation of cork
what advances in microscopy helped cell biology

solution_steps.explain: State the two tenets and Virchow's addition.
Note the contributions of Hooke, Leeuwenhoek, Schleiden and Schwann.
Confirm all functions of an organism rest on its cells.

concepts.title: Prokaryotic and Eukaryotic Cells
concepts.definition: Prokaryotic cells lack a true nucleus and membrane-bound organelles but carry a nucleoid, glycocalyx, cell wall, mesosomes and 70S ribosomes, whereas eukaryotic cells have a membrane-bound nucleus and organelles with 80S ribosomes.
concepts.key_idea: The fluid mosaic model of Singer and Nicolson describes the plasma membrane as a bilayer of phospholipids with proteins moving within it, and passive transport of water is osmosis.
question_patterns: describe the structure of a prokaryotic cell with mesosomes
explain the fluid mosaic model of the plasma membrane
how does passive transport differ from active transport across the membrane

solution_steps.explain: Look for a membrane-bound nucleus to separate prokaryotes from eukaryotes.
Note which membrane-bound organelles are present or absent.

concepts.title: Cell Organelles: Mitochondria, Plastids, Endomembranes and Nucleus
concepts.definition: Eukaryotic cells carry organelles such as the endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi complex, lysosomes, vacuoles, mitochondria as the site of aerobic respiration with double membranes and cristae, chloroplasts with grana and stroma among plastids, ribosomes for protein synthesis, and a nucleus with chromatin and nucleolus.
concepts.key_idea: The endomembrane system of ER, Golgi complex, lysosomes and vacuoles works in coordination, while semi-autonomous organelles like mitochondria and chloroplasts carry their own DNA and ribosomes.
question_patterns: describe the structure of mitochondria with cristae
what is the endomembrane system and its components
explain the structure of the nucleus with chromatin and nucleolus
why are mitochondria and chloroplast called semi autonomous organelles
state the functions of golgi complex and lysosomes

solution_steps.explain: Use structural markers like cristae, grana or cisternae to name the organelle.
Count the bounding membranes, single or double.
Match respiration, photosynthesis, packaging or digestion to the organelle.
